summary: Uttarādi Maṭha pontiff called Bhāvabodhācārya after his Bhāvabodha commentaries (e.g. on Madhva's Bṛhadāraṇyaka-bhāṣya); his brindāvana is at Tirukoilur.

name: Rahūgaṇa
summary: The king who forced Jaḍa Bharata to carry his palanquin and received from him instruction on the self beyond the body (BhP 5.10-13; the VP 2.13-16 version names the king of Sauvīra).

name: Rājānaka Lakṣmīrāma
summary: Later Kashmiri commentator on the Parātrīśikā.

name: Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha (author of the Spandavivṛti)
summary: Kashmiri commentator, a disciple of Utpaladeva, author of the Spandavivṛti (ascribing the kārikās to Kallaṭa) and of the Sarvatobhadra commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā.
notes: Distinct from tch:ramakantha (Rāmakaṇṭha II of the Śaiva Siddhānta).

name: Rāma (Dāśarathi)

tradition.text: Tretā yuga

summary: Prince of Ayodhyā, hero of the Rāmāyaṇa, called 'dharma embodied' (3.37.13); he goes into exile to keep his father's word, teaches Bharata on impermanence (2.105) and kingship (2.100), answers Jābāli that truth is the root of all (2.109), and vows protection to whoever seeks refuge (6.18.33); the Nārāyaṇīya names him among Nārāyaṇa's manifestations (12.326.78).
alt_summary: In U06's texts: the student of Vasiṣṭha in the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha (whose first book records his dispassion at sixteen); the teacher of Hanumān (Rāma-hṛdaya), Lakṣmaṇa (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 3.4 and the Rāma Gītā), Śabarī (the nine means of devotion) and Vibhīṣaṇa (Rāmcaritmānas); in the Śiva Gītā the recipient of Śiva's teaching. The Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa presents him as the supreme Brahman.

realization_account.text: In the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha Rāma, after Vasiṣṭha's teaching, rests in the supreme state (Nirvāṇa-prakaraṇa, opening chapters, e.g. MU 6.5 'rāghava-viśrānti'); the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa instead treats him as the Lord who never lost knowledge.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Rāma Tīrtha (Kaniyooru)
summary: Disciple of Madhva and, in the tradition's account, founder of the Kaniyooru maṭha, one of the eight maṭhas of Uḍupi that take turns in the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
notes: Founder-to-maṭha assignment recalled from memory; check against maṭha records.

name: Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha (II)
notes: Contribution from U08.
summary: Kashmirian Saiddhāntika exegete, son of Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha, who commented on the Kiraṇa, the Mataṅgapārameśvara and the Sārdhatriśatikālottara, and on works of Sadyojyoti, maintaining that liberation is the soul's becoming equal to Śiva, not identity with him.

name: Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha
summary: Kashmiri author credited with the Sarvatobhadra commentary on the Kashmir recension of the Gītā.
notes: Not identified here with the Saiddhāntika Rāmakaṇṭha (tch:ramakantha).

name: Ramana Maharshi
summary: In U06's context (recent reception): recommended the Ṛbhu Gītā, which was read aloud in his presence, and quoted the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha and the Aṣṭāvakra Gītā.

name: Rāmānanda Sarasvatī
summary: Author of the Yogamaṇiprabhā, a vṛtti that follows the bhāṣya; its colophon names him a paramahaṃsa pupil of Govindānanda.

name: Rāmānuja
summary: Author of a Gītā commentary reading it as teaching bhakti-yoga to Nārāyaṇa, supported by karma- and jñāna-yoga.
notes: U05's contribution only.

name: Rāmarudra Bhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Rāmarudrī, a gloss on the Muktāvalī continuing the Dinakarī.

name: Ṛbhu
summary: A mind-born son of Brahmā, knower of reality from birth, teacher of Nidāgha (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.15-16, verified); in the Śivarahasya he teaches Nidāgha the Ṛbhu Gītā received from Śiva.
alt_summary: Mind-born son of Brahmā (KūP 1.10.13 lists him with the Kumāras) who teaches his disciple Nidāgha the non-difference of all selves (VP 2.15-16) - told within Jaḍa Bharata's teaching; the Ṛbhu Gītā (U06) is a separate text.

name: Reṇukācārya (Revaṇasiddha)
summary: The first of the five ācāryas: the gaṇa Reṇuka who, cursed for leaping over his fellow gaṇa Dāruka in Śiva's assembly, emerged from the Someśvara liṅga at Kollipāki, taught Agastya the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi, and in the tradition founded the Rambhāpurī pīṭha at Bāḷehonnūr.

tradition.text: appears in every yuga; in the Kali age as Revaṇa/Reṇuka

realization_account.text: A pramatha created by Śiva (SSM 2.25–27), sent to earth for overstepping Dāruka (3.66–77), he appeared from the Someśvara liṅga at Kollipāki without human birth (3.83–84; 4.1), taught Agastya, visited Vibhīṣaṇa in Laṅkā, and returned into the liṅga (ch. 21).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Seat: Vīra-siṃhāsana at Rambhāpurī (low confidence on the siṃhāsana name).

name: Romaharṣaṇa

realization_account.text: The sūta disciple to whom Vyāsa gave the Purāṇa-saṃhitā; his own saṃhitā is the root (mūla) of the three made by his disciples (VP 3.6.16-18). BhP 12.7.5-7 names six paurāṇikas who learned from him.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The first paurāṇika: Vyāsa's disciple for the Purāṇa, reciter at Naimiṣa in several Purāṇas, father of Ugraśravas; the four root saṃhitās of the Purāṇa descend from him and his pupils.

name: Ṛṣabha

realization_account.text: Son of Nābhi and Merudevī, the eighth avatāra 'who showed the path honoured by all āśramas' (BhP 1.3.13); after teaching his sons that the human body is not for dog-like pleasures but for austerity (BhP 5.5.1-27), he lived as a naked avadhūta and gave up his body in a forest fire in Kuṭaka (BhP 5.5.28-5.6.8).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: In the Bhāgavata an avatāra of Viṣṇu and avadhūta-teacher; the same figure the Jains honour as the first Tīrthaṅkara. BhP 5.6.9 adds that a king named Arhat of Koṅka, Veṅka and Kuṭaka, imitating him, will spread a heterodox path in Kali (a polemical report).

name: Ṛṣabheśvara
summary: Named in the Yuktidīpikā's list of teachers through whom the doctrine passed between Pañcaśikha and Īśvarakṛṣṇa (on SK 71: Hārīta, Vāddhali, Kairāta, Paurika, Ṛṣabheśvara, Pañcādhikaraṇa, Patañjali, Vārṣagaṇya, Kauṇḍinya, Mūka and others). Not to be confused with the Jain Ṛṣabha.

name: Rūpa Bhavānī
summary: 17th-century Kashmiri Śaiva yoginī and poet in the line of Lal Ded, revered as a saint; her vākhs teach inner realization of Śiva.

tradition.text: 1621-1721 CE (traditional dates)

name: Śabarī
summary: A forest woman of low birth, disciple of the sage Mataṅga, who waited for Rāma; he teaches her that gender, caste and stage of life are no cause of devotion and gives her the nine means of devotion (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 3.10).

realization_account.text: After guiding Rāma to Sugrīva she entered the fire before him and, freed of all bonds made by ignorance, attained liberation by Rāma's grace (AR 3.10.39-42).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

alt_summary: An aged female ascetic (śramaṇī) of the Śabara people who served the sages of Mataṅga's hermitage, receives Rāma and ascends to the heavenly worlds (Rāmāyaṇa 3.73–74).

name: Ṣaḍakṣaradēva
summary: Seventeenth-century Kannada Vīraśaiva poet of campū works including the Rājaśēkharavilāsa and the Vṛṣabhēndravijaya.

name: Sadāśiva Brahmendra
places: Tamil country, Kāveri region (samādhi shrine at Nerur by tradition)
summary: Advaita avadhūta and composer of Sanskrit songs remembered in South Indian tradition; author of the Yogasudhākara on the Yoga Sūtra.
notes: Tradition makes him a pupil of Paramaśivendra Sarasvatī and credits him with further works (Brahma Sūtra vṛtti, Ātmavidyāvilāsa) — not verified here.

name: Sadyojyoti
notes: Contribution from U08 (catalogue: commentaries). Doctrine is U18's.
summary: Kashmirian theologian of the Śaiva Siddhānta, the earliest datable exegete of its scriptures; he commented on the Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṅgraha and wrote short doctrinal treatises (the Nareśvaraparīkṣā, Mokṣakārikā, Bhogakārikā and others).

name: Sāhib Kaul
summary: 17th-century Kashmiri Śaiva scholar-poet: a commentary on the Śiva Sūtra, the Devīnāmavilāsa, and works of Śrīvidyā ritual (Śrīvidyānityapaddhati).

name: Sakalēśa Mādarasa
summary: A chieftain-poet among the śaraṇas.

name: Samādhi (the merchant)
summary: A merchant cast out by his greedy family who still could not stop worrying about them; with Suratha he heard the Devī Māhātmya, and asked the Goddess not for wealth but for the knowledge that frees from attachment, which she granted (DM 13).

name: Samagāra Haraḷayya
summary: The cobbler śaraṇa whose son's marriage to the daughter of the brāhmaṇa Madhuvarasa precipitated the orthodox reaction and the upheaval at Kalyāṇa; both fathers were put to death by the king's order in the tradition's account.

name: Śambhunātha
summary: Abhinavagupta's teacher in the Kaula form of the Trika, from Jālandhara; the Tantrāloka credits him with the teaching of the seven ānandas of the breath (TĀ 5.52) and with the Kula ritual of ch. 29.
notes: Teacher-name Sumati(nātha) from TĀ ch. 1 as quoted in Jayaratha (low confidence on the relationship).

name: Śāṃśapāyana
summary: Disciple of Romaharṣaṇa and maker of one of the root Purāṇa-saṃhitās (VP 3.6.17-18); absent from the Bhāgavata's list of six paurāṇikas, which names Trayyāruṇi, Kaśyapa, Sāvarṇi, Akṛtavraṇa, Vaiśampāyana and Hārīta instead (BhP 12.7.5).

name: Sanaka
summary: Eldest of the four mind-born sons of Brahmā (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, Sanatkumāra), whose question on separating mind from the guṇas occasions the Haṃsa Gītā (Bhāgavata 11.13).

name: Sanandana
summary: Named by the Sāṃkhya Sūtra (6.69): 'the (owner–owned relation of puruṣa and prakṛti) is caused by the subtle body, says the teacher Sanandana'. Gauḍapāda (on SK 1, 43) names Sanaka, Sanandana (Sananda), Sanātana and Sanatkumāra among Brahmā's sons, in whom the dispositions arose naturally at sixteen.
notes: Whether the SS's teacher is the Kumāra of Purāṇic lore is not stated in the text.

name: Sanatkumāra
summary: Eldest of the four Kumāras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, Sanatkumāra), mind-born sons of Brahmā who refused to procreate and remained celibate knowers (VP 1.7; KūP 1.10.13-14); the first avatāra in BhP 1.3.6; with his brothers he instructs Nārada in the Nārada Purāṇa; the first Upapurāṇa bears his name (KūP 1.1.17).
alt_summary: Mind-born sage who, in the Vṛtra Gītā, teaches the greatness of Viṣṇu and the six colours of living beings (12.271).
notes: U05's contribution; his teaching in Chāndogya 7 is covered by U03.

name: Sanatsujāta
summary: An ever-youthful sage (kumāra) summoned by Vidura's thought, who teaches Dhṛtarāṣṭra that heedlessness is death and heedfulness immortality, and describes the brāhmaṇa, silence, the virtues and the shining Brahman seen by yogins (5.41–45).
notes: The tradition counts him among Brahmā's mind-born sons (not checked here).

name: Śāṇḍilya
notes: Contribution from U08.
summary: Sage who relates the Jayākhya's teaching to other sages; a Pāñcarātra account quoted by Śaṅkara (BSBh 2.2.45) says he took up this teaching after not finding the highest good in the four Vedas.

name: Saṅgamāditya
summary: Descendant of the Tryambaka siddhas (son of the fifteenth, who married a brāhmaṇa woman) who came wandering to Kashmir; great-great-grandfather of Somānanda (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.115-119).

name: Sañjaya

tradition.text: end of the Dvāpara yuga (the Bhārata war; Kali yuga traditionally from 3102 BCE)

summary: Dhṛtarāṣṭra's charioteer and counsellor, given divine sight by Vyāsa to see and report the battle (6.2); he narrates the Gītā to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and says he heard it 'by the grace of Vyāsa' directly from Kṛṣṇa (18.75).

name: Śaṅkara
summary: Author of the oldest extant Gītā commentary, which reads the Gītā as teaching liberation by knowledge of the self with renunciation, action serving to purify the mind; also credited with commentaries on the Sanatsujātīya and the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma.
notes: U05's contribution only (Gītā and epic works).
alt_summary: (Yoga unit contribution) The Pātañjalayogaśāstravivaraṇa, a sub-commentary on the Yoga-bhāṣya, is ascribed in its colophons to Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda, pupil of Govinda; whether this is the Advaita teacher is disputed.

name: Śaṅkara Miśra
summary: Mithilā scholar, author of the Upaskāra on the Vaiśeṣika Sūtra (the standard commentary until Candrānanda's was recovered) and of the Vādivinoda.

name: Ṣaṇmukhasvāmi
summary: A later Vīraśaiva ascetic and vacanakāra.

name: Sarvajña
summary: Wandering Kannada poet of the tripadi sayings, claimed by the Vīraśaiva tradition.
notes: Affiliation debated.

name: Śaśadhara
summary: Pre-Gaṅgeśa Naiyāyika, author of the Nyāyasiddhāntadīpa.

name: Satyadharma Tīrtha
summary: Uttarādi Maṭha pontiff of the 18th–19th centuries, remembered for glosses (ṭippaṇīs) on the Bhāgavata and on Madhva's commentaries; his brindāvana is at Holehonnur on the Tuṅgā.
notes: Titles of his works and his dates were not verified; no work entries are created (see REPORT gaps).

name: Satyadhyāna Tīrtha
summary: Uttarādi Maṭha pontiff of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, remembered for public debates with Advaita scholars and for promoting Dvaita learning.

name: Satyakka
summary: A woman śaraṇa remembered as a sweeper, whose vacanas affirm devotion over outward observance.

name: Satyanātha Tīrtha
summary: Uttarādi Maṭha pontiff and polemicist, author of the Abhinavāmṛta and other works titled 'Abhinava-'.

name: Śaunaka (of Naimiṣa)
summary: Head (kulapati) of the sages of the Naimiṣa forest, at whose twelve-year sacrifice Ugraśravas recites the Mahābhārata.
notes: A brāhmaṇa Śaunaka also instructs Yudhiṣṭhira at the start of the exile (3.2, the eightfold path of dharma at 3.2.71); the identity of the two is not asserted here.

name: Śaunaka (of Naimiṣa)
summary: The kulapati of the thousand-year sacrificial session (sattra) at the Naimiṣa forest who questions the Sūta in the frame of the Bhāgavata and other Purāṇas. Tradition's link to the Vedic Śaunakas is not asserted here.

name: Sāvarṇi (paurāṇika)
summary: Disciple of Romaharṣaṇa and maker of one of the root Purāṇa-saṃhitās (VP 3.6.17-18; BhP 12.7.5-7). Not to be confused with the Manu Sāvarṇi (the eighth Manu).

name: Sāvitrī
summary: Princess who chooses the doomed Satyavat, follows Yama when he takes Satyavat's life and wins it back through her words on dharma and the friendship of the good (3.277–283).

name: Senajit
summary: A king grieving for his son, consoled by a brāhmaṇa who cites Piṅgalā (12.168).

name: T. G. Siddappārādhya
summary: Twentieth-century author of a Vīraśaiva commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā (1965).

name: Siddhanañjeśa Śivācārya
summary: Author of the Sanskrit Śivasiddhāntacandrikā, of the Pūvalli Pañcavarṇa Bṛhanmaṭha.

name: Siddhanātha Śivācārya
summary: Father of Śivayogi Śivācārya, praised as 'crest-jewel of the Vīraśaivas' and a determiner of Śiva-siddhānta (SSM 1.17–20).

name: Siddharāma
summary: Siddharāma (Siddharāmēśvara) of Sonnalige, the builder of tanks and temples for Mallikārjuna who, in the tradition's account, was challenged by Allama, received liṅga-initiation from Cennabasava and joined the śaraṇas; vacanas signed Kapilasiddhamallikārjuna.

realization_account.text: A karmayogin devoted to Mallikārjuna of Śrīśaila, he was met at Sonnalige by Allama, who mocked his works; he went to Kalyāṇa, received liṅga-initiation and later attained union at Sonnalige.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: The Tattvapradīpikā's introduction calls the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi's author a member of the lineage of Siddharāma, 'born from the glance of Revaṇasiddha' (e-text M00207).

name: Śikhidhvaja
summary: King of Mālava who renounced his kingdom for forest austerities but found no peace until his wife Cūḍālā, disguised as Kumbha, taught him that renunciation of everything includes renunciation of the mind that renounces.

realization_account.text: After giving up even his ascetic's belongings and his body-identification he entered a long samādhi, awoke liberated and returned to rule with Cūḍālā.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ṣimānanda Dīkṣita
alt_names: Kṣemānanda (identification suggested by the e-text's editor, uncertain)
summary: Author of the Sāṃkhyatattvavivecana on the Tattvasamāsa; by his own account son of Raghunandana, a Kānyakubja brahmin living at Iṣṭikāpura.

name: Siṅgirāja
summary: Kannada poet of the Amala Basavarāja Cāritra.

name: Sītā
summary: Daughter of Janaka of Mithilā and Rāma's wife; the Rāmāyaṇa's exemplar of the devoted wife, taught by Anasūyā (2.117–119).
alt_summary: In the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa she instructs Hanumān (1.1.31-43): Rāma is the non-dual Brahman and she is primal nature (mūlaprakṛti), the agent of all the deeds superimposed on him.

name: Rājānaka Śitikaṇṭha
summary: Author of the Mahānayaprakāśa on the Krama in Old Kashmiri with a Sanskrit commentary.

name: Śiva
summary: In U06's texts: speaker of the Īśvara Gītā (to the sages), the Śiva Gītā (to Rāma), the Guru Gītā (to Pārvatī) and the Rudra Gītā (to the Pracetās); narrator of the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa to Pārvatī; in the Mokṣopāya he teaches Vasiṣṭha the true worship of the divine as consciousness (MU 6.31-46).
alt_summary: In the epic, Śiva teaches Umā dharma (13.126–134), is named as the proclaimer of the Pāśupata knowledge (12.337.62), grants Arjuna the Pāśupata weapon after testing him as a hunter (3.38–41), and is praised with a thousand names (13.14–17); 'among the Rudras I am Śaṃkara' (BhG 10.23); Rudra and Nārāyaṇa are one being made twofold (12.328.24).
notes: U05's contribution (the epic account).

name: Śivāditya
summary: Author of the Saptapadārthī, which expounds the categories as seven (adding absence) and fuses Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika.

name: Śivagaṇaprasādi Mahādēvayya
summary: Compiler of a redaction of the Śūnyasampādane.

name: Śivāgrayogin
summary: Late Saiddhāntika author of the Śaivasiddhāntaparibhāṣā and ritual works.

name: Śivakumāra Svāmi (Siddhagaṅgā)
summary: Head of the Siddhagaṅgā maṭha, known for dāsōha — daily free feeding and schooling of thousands of children of every background.

name: Śivayogi Śivācārya
summary: Compiler of the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi, son of the Vīraśaiva ācārya Siddhanātha in the line of Muddadeva (SSM 1.13–24), who composed it from the Āgamas 'from Kāmika to Vātula' and the Śaiva Purāṇas without contradicting the Vedic path (1.25–27).

scholarly.text: debated: placed variously between the 12th and 15th c.

notes: The Tattvapradīpikā places him in the lineage of Siddharāma; the SSM colophon also styles the composition Reṇukācārya's.

name: Śivopādhyāya
summary: 18th-century Kashmiri commentator who completed the commentary on the Vijñāna Bhairava from v. 24, where Kṣemarāja's breaks off.

name: Somānanda
summary: Founder of the Pratyabhijñā philosophy with the Śivadṛṣṭi; he traced his descent from the mind-born siddhas of Durvāsas' Tryambaka line (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.107-122). Teacher of Utpaladeva; also wrote a (lost) commentary on the Parātrīśikā cited by Abhinavagupta.

realization_account.text: Heir of a line of siddhas born of the mind of Durvāsas, descended through the fifteenth who married, whose son came to Kashmir.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Somaśambhu
summary: Author of the Kriyākāṇḍakramāvalī (Somaśambhupaddhati, 1095/96), the most influential manual of Śaiva Siddhānta ritual, covering daily worship, initiation, consecration and funeral rites.

name: Sri Aurobindo
summary: Author of the Essays on the Gita (1916–20).
notes: U05's contribution only; his lineage is owned by U52.

name: Śrīdhara Svāmin
summary: The most influential commentator on the Bhāgavata and the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (and on the Gītā, Subodhinī), a renunciant whose non-dualism is devotional (Narasiṃha-bhakti); later Vaiṣṇava schools build on or argue with his readings.
alt_summary: Advaita commentator who emphasizes devotion; author of the Subodhinī on the Gītā (and of the Bhāvārthadīpikā on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa).

name: Śrīdhara
summary: Bengali author of the Nyāyakandalī on the Padārthadharmasaṅgraha, dated 991 CE in its colophon. (Distinct from Śrīdhara Svāmin, the Bhāgavata commentator.)

name: Śrīkaṇṭhabhaṭṭa
summary: Son of Mahādevabhaṭṭa, from whom Bhāskara received the Śiva Sūtra teaching (Vārttika 1.8).
notes: Distinct from tch:srikantha (Śaiva Vedānta) and tch:srikanthanatha (mythic).

name: Śrīkaṇṭha(nātha)
summary: The form of Śiva who, wandering on Mount Kailāsa when the Śaiva secrets had been lost at the start of the Kali age, descended for grace and commanded the sage Durvāsas to keep the scripture from being cut off (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.107-110).

realization_account.text: A form of Śiva himself.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Distinct from tch:srikantha (the Śaiva Vedāntin) and tch:srikanthabhatta (Bhāskara's teacher).

name: Śrīnivāsa Dīkṣita
notes: Self-description checked in sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/gretil_devanAgarI/1_sanskr/4_rellit/vaisn/srinivasamakhi_vedantadesika_dasavidhahetunirupana.md (GRETIL, input by U. Hüsken) (DHN 1.15–20). Date not established here.
summary: Vaikhānasa scholar ('Śrīnivāsamakhin', titled Vedāntadeśika), of the Kauśika lineage, son of Govindācārya and devotee of Veṅkaṭeśa, author of the Tātparyacintāmaṇi commentary containing the Daśavidhahetunirūpaṇa.

name: Śrīnivāsa Tīrtha
summary: Mādhva commentator, author of the Ṛgarthoddhāra on the Ṛgveda hymns covered by Madhva's Ṛgbhāṣya.

name: Śrīpādarāja
summary: Ascetic of Mulbagal (monastic name Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Tīrtha), teacher of Vyāsatīrtha in the śāstras, author of the Vāgvajra on the Nyāyasudhā, and, in the tradition, the 'grandfather' of the Kannada Haridāsa movement, composing songs with the signature Raṅgaviṭhala.

name: Śrīpati Paṇḍita
summary: Author of the Śrīkarabhāṣya, the Vīraśaiva commentary on the Brahmasūtra that names the doctrine Śakti-viśiṣṭādvaita (philosophy owned by U16; this entry records the Vīraśaiva lineage link).

name: Śrīvallabha
summary: Author of the Nyāyalīlāvatī, an independent Vaiśeṣika treatise. (Distinct from Vallabha of the Puṣṭimārga.)

name: Sudhīndra Tīrtha
summary: Successor of Vijayīndra Tīrtha and the teacher who gave renunciation to Rāghavendra Tīrtha.

name: Śuka

realization_account.text: Born liberated and absorbed in Brahman, he was drawn by the qualities of Hari to learn the Bhāgavata from his father (BhP 1.7.9-11); an avadhūta wandering naked whom women did not notice as a man (BhP 1.4.5); he recited the Bhāgavata to Parīkṣit in seven days and ended with the non-dual instruction 'I am Brahman, the supreme abode' (BhP 12.5.11).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Vyāsa's son, the paramahaṃsa narrator of the Bhāgavata to King Parīkṣit on the bank of the Gaṅgā; one of the twelve 'great ones' (mahājana) who know the dharma of devotion (BhP 6.3.20, 'vaiyāsaki').
alt_summary: Son of Vyāsa, instructed by his father (12.224–247) and by Janaka at Mithilā (12.312–313); he rises by yoga from the peak of Kailāsa into the sky and attains the highest state, while Vyāsa grieves after him (12.318–320).
notes: U05's contribution; his role as reciter of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa is covered by U07. The Janaka who teaches Śuka is referenced by the registry id tch:janaka without asserting identity with the Upaniṣadic king.

name: Sulabhā
summary: A female mendicant (bhikṣukī) practising the dharma of yoga who wanders the earth alone; doubting king Janaka's liberation, she enters his mind by yoga ('sattva by sattva', 12.308.16) and answers his rebuke with a discourse showing that his attachments remain (12.308).

name: Sūle Saṅkavva
summary: A courtesan who became a śaraṇa and vacanakāra.

name: Sumati ('Jaḍa')
summary: Son of a Bhārgava brahmin who behaved like a dullard (jaḍa) because he remembered past births; he told his father how beings are born, die, travel to Yama and suffer in hell (MkP 10-15), the account the wise birds relate to Jaimini.

name: Sumati(nātha)
summary: Kaula teacher praised in the Tantrāloka as the one whose wisdom dispelled Śambhunātha's darkness; Abhinavagupta's teacher's teacher.

name: Suratha
summary: A king of the Caitra line, deposed by enemies and ministers; after hearing the Devī Māhātmya he worshipped the Goddess for three years and received his kingdom back and the boon of becoming Sāvarṇi, the eighth Manu (DM 13; MkP 93.17).

name: Surendra Tīrtha
summary: Pontiff of the Kumbhakonam maṭha who, in the tradition's account, received Vijayīndra Tīrtha from Vyāsatīrtha as his successor.

name: Syūmaraśmi
summary: A sage who, entering a sacrificial cow, challenges Kapila's exclamation at the Vedas (12.260–262).

name: Toṇṭada Siddhaliṅga
summary: Fifteenth-century Vīraśaiva ascetic of Yeḍiyūr whose Ṣaṭsthalajñānasārāmṛta renewed the vacana tradition; teacher of a line of renunciant (virakta) masters.

name: Toṇṭadārya
summary: A renunciant Vīraśaiva teacher (parivrājakācārya) to whom the Kaivalyasāra's exposition of the 101 sthalas is ascribed.
notes: Relation to Toṇṭada Siddhaliṅga (tch:tontada-siddhalinga) not settled here.

name: Trilocana
summary: Naiyāyika named by Vācaspati Miśra as his teacher ('following the path led by my teacher Trilocana', Tātparyaṭīkā on NS 1.1.4); his works are known only from citations.

name: Trilocanaśiva
summary: South Indian Saiddhāntika author of the Siddhāntasārāvalī, a verse digest of ritual.

name: Trivikrama Paṇḍitācārya
summary: An Advaita scholar who, in the tradition's account, debated Madhva for many days at Viṣṇumaṅgala (Kasaragod) and became his disciple. He wrote the Tattvapradīpa, the first commentary on Madhva's Brahmasūtrabhāṣya, and the Vāyustuti praising Vāyu's three avatāras; his son Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya wrote the Sumadhvavijaya.

name: Tryambakāditya
summary: Mind-born son of Durvāsas who received the Śaiva secrets, went to a cave named Tryambaka and in turn created a mind-born son; fourteen such siddhas followed (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.111-114). The lineage was known as Tryambaka, 'Terambā' in the local language (7.121).

name: Tulādhāra
summary: A merchant of Vārāṇasī who teaches the ascetic Jājali that the eternal dharma is friendliness and non-injury to all beings (12.253–256).

name: Tulsīdās
summary: In U06's texts: author of the Rāmcaritmānas passages known as the Lakṣmaṇa Gītā and the Vibhīṣaṇa Gītā; he drew on the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa (Śiva-Pārvatī frame, Śabarī's nine devotions).

name: Turaimaṅkalam Śivaprakāśar
summary: Tamil Vīraśaiva poet who rendered the Prabhuliṅgalīle into Tamil.

name: Turugāhi Rāmaṇṇa
summary: A cowherd śaraṇa and vacanakāra.

name: Udayana

tradition.text: Lakṣaṇāvalī dated Śaka 906 = 984 CE by its own closing verse

summary: Called simply 'the Ācārya' by later Naiyāyikas; the great defender of Īśvara (Nyāyakusumāñjali) and of the self against the Buddhists (Ātmatattvaviveka), commentator on Vācaspati (Pariśuddhi) and on Praśastapāda (Kiraṇāvalī), author of the Lakṣaṇāvalī. He joined Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika and is regarded as the bridge between old and new Nyāya.
notes: Hagiographic tradition (low confidence): denied entry to the Jagannātha temple at Puri, he is said to have addressed the Lord: 'Drunk with lordship you disregard me; when the Buddhists come, your existence depends on me.'

name: Uddhava
summary: Kṛṣṇa's cousin, counsellor and devotee; recipient of the Uddhava Gītā. Earlier Kṛṣṇa sent him to Vraja, where he learned from the gopīs' love (Bhāgavata 10.46-47). At the end of the teaching he departs for Badarikāśrama (11.29).

realization_account.text: Having heard the teaching, Uddhava, freed of doubt, went to Badarikāśrama to live it out (Bhāgavata 11.29).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

alt_summary: Kṛṣṇa's friend and counsellor, sent to Vraja with Kṛṣṇa's message to the gopīs, whose love in separation he came to revere (BhP 10.46-47); later the recipient of the Uddhava Gītā (BhP 11.7-29, owned by U06).

name: Uddyotakara
summary: Author of the Nyāyavārttika, written to remove the 'ignorance created by bad reasoners' — Dignāga and others, as Vācaspati glosses. The colophon of his work calls him a Pāśupata teacher.
notes: The Pāśupata affiliation rests on the colophon as usually reported (moderate confidence).

name: Ugraśravas Sauti

tradition.text: end of the Dvāpara yuga (the Bhārata war; Kali yuga traditionally from 3102 BCE)

summary: Son of Lomaharṣaṇa, the bard who retells the Mahābhārata, as heard at Janamejaya's sacrifice, to the sages assembled for Śaunaka's twelve-year sacrifice in the Naimiṣa forest (1.1).
alt_summary: Son of Romaharṣaṇa, the Sūta who recites the Bhāgavata and other Purāṇas to Śaunaka and the sages of the Naimiṣa forest (having heard the Bhāgavata from Śuka at Parīkṣit's assembly); he learned all four root saṃhitās (BhP 12.7.6).

name: Ulūka (Sāṃkhya teacher)
summary: Named in the Māṭhara Vṛtti (on SK 71) among those through whom the knowledge came from Pañcaśikha to Īśvarakṛṣṇa: Bhārgava, Ulūka, Vālmīki, Hārīta, Devala and others. 'Ulūka' is also a name of the Vaiśeṣika founder Kaṇāda; no identity is implied.

name: Umā (Pārvatī)
summary: Śiva's consort, who questions him on dharma and herself expounds the dharma of women in the Anuśāsana (13.126–134).

name: Umāpati Śivācārya
notes: Contribution from U08 (Sanskrit Āgama works); Tamil works are U18's.
summary: Cidambaram Saiddhāntika who wrote in Tamil and Sanskrit; in Sanskrit he commented on the Pauṣkarāgama's jñānapāda and compiled the Śataratnasaṅgraha of Āgama verses.

name: Upamanyu
summary: The Śaiva sage who, having won Śiva's favour as a child through austerity, gives Kṛṣṇa Pāśupata initiation and teaches him Śaiva doctrine, worship, the pañcākṣara and yoga in the Vāyavīya Saṃhitā (ŚiP 7.2) and in LiP 1.107.
alt_summary: A sage devoted to Śiva who teaches Kṛṣṇa the thousand names of Śiva first revealed by Taṇḍi (13.14–17).

name: Uparicara Vasu
summary: A king devoted to Nārāyaṇa who performed a horse sacrifice without slaughter; when he sided with the gods that 'aja' in the injunction means a goat, he fell, and was restored by his devotion (12.322–324).

name: Upendra Tīrtha
summary: Disciple of Madhva and, in the tradition's account, founder of the Puttige maṭha, one of the eight maṭhas of Uḍupi that take turns in the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
notes: Founder-to-maṭha assignment recalled from memory; check against maṭha records.

name: Uriliṅgadēva
summary: A śaraṇa teacher whose disciple and successor Uriliṅgapeddi came from the margins of society.

name: Uriliṅgapeddi
summary: A former thief of low-caste birth who became Uriliṅgadēva's disciple, successor and a vacanakāra.

name: Uśanas (Śukra)
summary: Preceptor of the asuras, who questions Vṛtra (12.270); 'among poets I am Uśanas' (BhG 10.37).

name: Utpala Vaiṣṇava
notes: Quotations noted in the introduction to the JS edition (local e-text).
summary: Kashmirian Vaiṣṇava author of the Spandapradīpikā, a commentary on the Spandakārikā that quotes Pāñcarātra saṃhitās (the Jayākhya, the Ahirbudhnya), furnishing an early date-limit for them.
alt_summary: A Kashmiri Vaiṣṇava (Pāñcarātra) scholar who wrote the Spandapradīpikā, a commentary on the Spandakārikā ascribing it to Kallaṭa - an instance of Vaiṣṇava engagement with Spanda.

name: Utpaladeva
summary: Son of Udayākara (ĪPK 4.18) and disciple of Somānanda; systematized the Pratyabhijñā in the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā with a short and a long commentary, wrote the Siddhitrayī and the devotional hymns of the Śivastotrāvalī.

realization_account.text: His hymns present devotion as the relish of an identity with Śiva already recognized.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vācaspati Miśra

scholarly.text: 9th or 10th c. CE (Nyāyasūcīnibandha dated 898 of an era read as Vikrama = 841 CE or Śaka = 976 CE)

summary: Polymath of Mithilā who commented on every Vedic school; for Nyāya he wrote the Tātparyaṭīkā — rescuing Uddyotakara's 'aged cows' from the mire of bad commentaries — and the Nyāyasūcīnibandha, which fixed the sūtra text. He reads 'avyapadeśya' and 'vyavasāyātmaka' in NS 1.1.4 as indeterminate and determinate perception, following his teacher Trilocana.
notes: His non-Nyāya works belong to U09, U10, U12 and U13.
alt_summary: (Yoga unit contribution) Author of the Tattvavaiśāradī, the standard sub-commentary on Vyāsa's Yoga-bhāṣya; a polymath who also commented on Nyāya, Sāṃkhya, Mīmāṃsā and Advaita texts.
U09 contribution: author of the Sāṃkhyatattvakaumudī, the standard later commentary on the SK; the Yuktidīpikā's colophon also names him, an ascription scholars reject.

name: Vāddhali
summary: Named in the Yuktidīpikā's list of teachers through whom the doctrine passed between Pañcaśikha and Īśvarakṛṣṇa (on SK 71: Hārīta, Vāddhali, Kairāta, Paurika, Ṛṣabheśvara, Pañcādhikaraṇa, Patañjali, Vārṣagaṇya, Kauṇḍinya, Mūka and others). The reading of the name in the e-text is uncertain.

name: Vādirāja Tīrtha

tradition.text: the tradition gives him 120 years, 1480–1600

realization_account.text: The tradition regards Vādirāja as a ṛju soul — one of the class destined for the highest offices — and as a future Vāyu (bhāvi-samīra).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Pontiff of the Sode maṭha (Uḍupi), worshipper of Hayagrīva, poet and polemicist: author of the Yuktimallikā, the Tīrthaprabandha, the Rukmiṇīśavijaya and a commentary on the Mahābhārata, and of Kannada songs signed 'Hayavadana'. The tradition credits him with making the Uḍupi paryāya of Kṛṣṇa worship a two-year turn.
notes: The 1522 start of the two-year paryāya and the 'bhāvi-samīra' belief are recalled at moderate/low confidence.

name: Vaiśampāyana

tradition.text: end of the Dvāpara yuga (the Bhārata war; Kali yuga traditionally from 3102 BCE)

summary: Vyāsa's disciple who recites the Mahābhārata to king Janamejaya during the snake sacrifice; the narrator of the Nārāyaṇīya to Janamejaya.

name: Vālmīki

tradition.text: Tretā yuga, contemporary of Rāma

summary: The first poet (ādikavi), author of the Rāmāyaṇa; told Rāma's story by Nārada (1.1), he utters the first śloka in grief at a hunter's killing of a krauñca bird (1.2.15–18) and teaches the poem to Kuśa and Lava.
alt_summary: In U06's texts: the traditional author of the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha / Mokṣopāya, who opens it by telling Bharadvāja that Brahmā sent him to complete a Rāmāyaṇa of liberation (MU 1.1).

name: Vālmīki (Sāṃkhya teacher)
summary: Named in the Māṭhara Vṛtti (on SK 71) among those through whom the knowledge came from Pañcaśikha to Īśvarakṛṣṇa: Bhārgava, Ulūka, Vālmīki, Hārīta, Devala and others. No identification with the poet of the Rāmāyaṇa is implied.

name: Vāmadeva
summary: Author of the Janmamaraṇavicāra on birth and death.

name: Vāmana Tīrtha
summary: Disciple of Madhva and, in the tradition's account, founder of the Shirur maṭha, one of the eight maṭhas of Uḍupi that take turns in the worship of Kṛṣṇa.
notes: Founder-to-maṭha assignment recalled from memory; check against maṭha records.

name: Vāmanadatta
summary: Author of the Svabodhodayamañjarī.

name: Varadarāja (Kṛṣṇadāsa)
summary: Author of a second Śivasūtravārttika, following Kṣemarāja.

name: Varadarāja
summary: Author of the Tārkikarakṣā, a Nyāya manual with auto-commentary.

name: Vardhamāna Upādhyāya
summary: Son of Gaṅgeśa; wrote Prakāśa commentaries on Udayana's works (Kusumāñjali, Kiraṇāvalī) and on his father's Tattvacintāmaṇi.

name: Vareṇya
summary: The king to whom Gajānana teaches the Gaṇeśa Gītā; in the Gaṇeśa Purāṇa Gaṇeśa had been born in his house.

name: Varṣāditya
summary: Son of Saṅgamāditya in Somānanda's lineage (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.119).

name: Vārṣagaṇya
alt_names: Vṛṣagaṇa (a related name in the Yuktidīpikā and in the Chinese Life of Vasubandhu)
summary: Early Sāṃkhya teacher. The Yoga Bhāṣya (on YS 3.53) cites him by name: there is no difference at the root, since there is no difference of form, separation or kind. The Yuktidīpikā (on SK 22) reports his views that mahat arises directly from pradhāna and that the subtle elements are cumulative; it lists him among the teachers before Īśvarakṛṣṇa (on SK 71). Some scholars ascribe the Ṣaṣṭitantra to him.

name: Varuṇaśiva
summary: Author of the Varuṇapaddhati, a Siddhānta ritual manual.

name: Vasiṣṭha
summary: In U06's texts: the family priest of the Ikṣvākus who, at Viśvāmitra's request, teaches the despondent young Rāma the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha / Mokṣopāya; within it he recounts his own learning from Brahmā, from the crow Bhuśuṇḍa and from Śiva.
alt_summary: Ancient seer, family priest of the Ikṣvākus; in the Mokṣadharma he teaches Karāla Janaka the Sāṃkhya-Yoga doctrine of the 24 principles, the 25th and the 26th (12.291–296); in the Rāmāyaṇa he is Rāma's preceptor.
notes: His teaching in the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha is covered by U06.

name: Vāsudeva Sārvabhauma
summary: Navadvīpa scholar who, on the tradition's account, studied in Mithilā and brought the Tattvacintāmaṇi to Navadvīpa (by memory, since copying was not permitted); teacher of Raghunātha Śiromaṇi in the same account; later a court scholar at Puri, where the Gauḍīya hagiographies place his meeting with Caitanya.
notes: Most details are the tradition's account (low confidence).

name: Vasugupta
summary: The Kashmiri teacher to whom the Śiva Sūtras were revealed and from whom the Spanda tradition descends; Kṣemarāja also makes him the author of the Spandakārikā.

realization_account.text: Paramaśiva, wishing the secret tradition not to be cut off, favoured him in a dream and told him of a secret on a great rock on Mahādeva mountain; on waking he found the rock, which turned over at the touch of his hand, and received the sūtras (Kṣemarāja). In Bhāskara's account the sūtras appeared to him 'by a siddha's command'.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vātsyāyana
summary: Author of the Nyāyabhāṣya, the first extant commentary on the Nyāya Sūtra; criticized by Dignāga. Not to be identified (on the scholarly account) with Vātsyāyana Mallanāga of the Kāmasūtra.

name: Vedānta Deśika
notes: Contribution from U08.
summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava ācārya (Veṅkaṭanātha) whose Pāñcarātrarakṣā defends and expounds the Pāñcarātra.
alt_summary: Author of the Tātparyacandrikā on Rāmānuja's Gītābhāṣya.

name: Vibhīṣaṇa
summary: Rāvaṇa's righteous brother who took refuge with Rāma; the Rāmcaritmānas's 'chariot of dharma' teaching is addressed to him.
alt_summary: Rāvaṇa's brother who leaves him and takes refuge with Rāma; Rāma accepts him with the vow to protect all who seek refuge (6.18.33).

name: Vicakhnu
summary: A king who, pitying the animals at a sacrifice, proclaims non-violence as the highest dharma (12.257).

name: Vidura

tradition.text: end of the Dvāpara yuga (the Bhārata war; Kali yuga traditionally from 3102 BCE)

realization_account.text: An embodiment of Dharma; his death by yoga, entering Yudhiṣṭhira, is narrated at 15.33.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Half-brother of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu, born of a śūdra woman; Dharma incarnate through Māṇḍavya's curse (1.100.28). He counsels Dhṛtarāṣṭra (Viduranīti, 5.33–40) and, declaring that as one born of a śūdra womb he will not speak beyond this, calls Sanatsujāta to teach the higher knowledge (5.41.5); consoles him after the war (11.2–7); dies in the forest by entering Yudhiṣṭhira's body limb by limb and breath by breath (15.33.25).

name: Vidyādhirāja Tīrtha
summary: Jayatīrtha's successor; the tradition dates the later division of the lines (towards the Uttarādi, Rāghavendra and Vyāsarāja maṭhas) from his disciples.

name: Vidyāraṇya
summary: In U06's context: his Jīvanmuktiviveka builds its account of liberation while living largely on quotations from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha (e.g. the weakening of latent tendencies and the dissolution of mind).

name: Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha
summary: Pontiff of the Pejavara maṭha (Uḍupi) and author of the Padaratnāvalī, the standard Mādhva commentary on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

name: Vijayīndra Tīrtha
summary: Pontiff at Kumbhakonam, trained by Vyāsatīrtha; a prolific polemicist (the tradition credits him with over a hundred works) who answered Appayya Dīkṣita's critiques of Madhva and commented on the Nyāyāmṛta.

name: Vijñānabhikṣu

scholarly.text: second half of the 16th c. CE

summary: (Yoga unit contribution) Vedāntin of 'non-separation' (avibhāga) who commented on Yoga, Sāṃkhya and the Brahma Sūtra. In the Yogavārttika he reads Yoga theistically, calls the bhāṣya 'the essence of all the Veda', argues for the mutual reflection of consciousness and buddhi (YV 1.7), gives his own account of the samprajñāta samādhis (YV 1.17) and holds that knowledge of the Supreme Lord is the swift cause of liberation (YV 1.51).
alt_summary: Commentator who revived Sāṃkhya-Yoga in a theistic, Vedānta-reconciling form: his Sāṃkhyapravacanabhāṣya on the Sāṃkhya Sūtra, his manual Sāṃkhyasāra, and his Yogavārttika on the Yoga Bhāṣya; he also wrote a Vedānta commentary on the Brahma Sūtra (Vijñānāmṛtabhāṣya).

name: Vikhanas

realization_account.text: Vikhanas is Nārāyaṇa himself (or the four-faced Brahmā born from him), so that his Sūtra is the first and best of sūtras.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Checked in sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/ebhAratI-sampat/AgamaH/vaikhAnasam/bhRgumaharShiH/kriyAdhikAraH.md (Kriyādhikāra, eBhāratī/NSU Tirupati) and sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/gretil_devanAgarI/1_sanskr/4_rellit/vaisn/srinivasamakhi_vedantadesika_dasavidhahetunirupana.md (GRETIL, input by U. Hüsken).
summary: Founding sage of the Vaikhānasas and author of their Sūtra; the tradition identifies him with Brahmā born of Nārāyaṇa, or with Nārāyaṇa himself, and salutes him as the one 'whose father is Nārāyaṇa, whose mother is Haripriyā, whose disciples are Bhṛgu and the other sages' (Kriyādhikāra 1.1).

name: Vimalaśiva
notes: From the Muktabodha catalogue description (sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/mukta/muktabodha_metadata.json (Muktabodha catalogue descriptions)).
summary: Saiddhāntika author of the Vimalāvatī on ritual, who took a lifelong vow of residence in Vārāṇasī.

name: Vindhyavāsin
summary: Sāṃkhya teacher whose distinctive views the Yuktidīpikā records: from mahat arise six non-specifics (ahaṃkāra and the five subtle elements); the organs are eleven and all-pervading; the functions of saṅkalpa, abhimāna and adhyavasāya are one; there is no subtle body — birth is the organs' functioning at the seed-place and death its abandonment; even the supreme sage's knowledge is acquired, not innate. Kumārila reports that he did not accept an intermediate body. Paramārtha's Life of Vasubandhu tells that the Sāṃkhya master Vindhyavāsa, pupil of Vṛṣagaṇa, defeated Vasubandhu's teacher Buddhamitra in debate before a king at Ayodhyā.
notes: Kumārila's report (Ślokavārttika, Ātmavāda section) and the Chinese biography details are recalled, not checked.

name: Virūpākṣanātha
summary: Author of the Virūpākṣapañcāśikā, probably South Indian.

name: Viṣṇu Tīrtha (Sode)
summary: Disciple of Madhva and, in the tradition's account, founder of the Sode maṭha, one of the eight maṭhas of Uḍupi that take turns in the worship of Kṛṣṇa. He was Madhva's younger brother; the tradition also derives the Subrahmaṇya maṭha from him and remembers his austerities.
notes: Founder-to-maṭha assignment recalled from memory; check against maṭha records.

name: Viṣṇucitta
summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava author of the Viṣṇucittīya commentary on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (dating not checked in this sweep).

name: Viśvāmitra
summary: In U06's texts: the sage whose request for Rāma's help occasions the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha and who is present throughout Vasiṣṭha's teaching.
alt_summary: Royal sage who takes the young Rāma to protect his sacrifice and teaches him (Bālakāṇḍa); in the Āpaddharma, during a famine, he takes a dog's haunch from an outcaste, arguing the case for survival (12.139).

name: Viśvanātha Cakravartin
summary: Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava theologian, author of the Sārārthavarṣiṇī on the Gītā.

name: Viśvanātha Nyāyapañcānana

scholarly.text: first half of the 17th c. CE

summary: Bengali Naiyāyika, author of the Bhāṣāpariccheda (Kārikāvalī) with its auto-commentary the Siddhāntamuktāvalī — opening with a salutation to Kṛṣṇa — and of a Nyāyasūtravṛtti.

name: Viśvārādhya
summary: One of the five ācāryas of the Pañcācārya tradition, founder in its account of the Kāśī pīṭha (Jaṅgamavāḍī maṭha, Vārāṇasī).

tradition.text: appears in every yuga under different names

notes: Emergence from the Viśvanātha liṅga at Kāśī and seat name Jñāna-siṃhāsana: low confidence.

name: Viśvāvasu
summary: A Gandharva, versed in Vedānta, who puts twenty-four questions and a twenty-fifth on reasoning to Yājñavalkya (12.306.27).

name: Viśveśa Tīrtha
summary: Pontiff of the Pejavara maṭha (Uḍupi) in the 20th and early 21st centuries, who presided over the Uḍupi Kṛṣṇa paryāya five times.

name: Vivasvat (the Sun)
summary: The first recipient of the imperishable yoga from Kṛṣṇa, who passed it to Manu (BhG 4.1).

name: Vivekananda
summary: In U06's context (recent reception): he often quoted the Avadhūta Gītā and the Aṣṭāvakra Gītā; Ramakrishna is remembered as having had him read the Aṣṭāvakra Saṃhitā.

name: Voḍhu
summary: One of the seven great sages, sons of Brahmā, in the verse quoted by Gauḍapāda on SK 1 (Sanaka, Sananda, Sanātana, Āsuri, Kapila, Voḍhu, Pañcaśikha).

name: Vopadeva
summary: Grammarian (Mugdhabodha) who wrote works on the Bhāgavata (the Muktāphala and the Harilīlāmṛta, the latter a summary of its contents); opponents of the Bhāgavata's status later claimed he composed the Bhāgavata itself, a claim its defenders reject (dsp:which-bhagavata-is-the-mahapurana).

name: Vṛtra
summary: The defeated asura whose equanimity is praised and who is taught by Sanatkumāra about Viṣṇu and the six colours of beings (12.270–271).

name: Vyāsa (Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana)

tradition.text: end of the Dvāpara yuga (the Bhārata war; Kali yuga traditionally from 3102 BCE)

realization_account.text: Presented as a seer who knows past, present and future, able to grant divine sight and to foresee the war's outcome; identified with the earlier Apāntaratamas (12.337.54).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Son of Parāśara and Satyavatī, in the tradition the arranger of the Vedas and author of the Mahābhārata; grandfather of the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas; gives Sañjaya divine sight, teaches his son Śuka (12.224–247), and tells that in a former birth he was Apāntaratamas, the Veda-teacher born of Nārāyaṇa's word, reborn in Vasiṣṭha's line (12.337.38–54). The Gītā names him among those who proclaim Kṛṣṇa supreme (10.13) and 'among sages I am Vyāsa' (10.37).
alt_summary: (Yoga unit contribution) For the Yoga tradition, the author of the Yogabhāṣya, the oldest commentary on the Yoga Sūtra. Vijñānabhikṣu calls him Vedavyāsa and Bādarāyaṇa and says he spoke 'the essence of all the Veda under the guise of the Yoga-bhāṣya'; Nārāyaṇatīrtha also names the bhāṣyakāra Bādarāyaṇa. Modern scholars doubt the identification; several ascribe the bhāṣya to Patañjali himself.

In the Purāṇic tradition the compiler of the eighteen Purāṇas (and Upapurāṇas through his disciples, KūP 1.1.280), who gave the Purāṇa-saṃhitā to his sūta disciple Romaharṣaṇa (VP 3.6.15-16) and the Bhāgavata to his son Śuka.

In U06's texts: the traditional author of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Uddhava and Kapila Gītās), the Devī Bhāgavata (Devī Gītā), the Kūrma Purāṇa and, as part of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; the speaker of the Vyāsa Gītā.

name: Vyāsa Rāmācārya
summary: Mādhva scholar who wrote the Nyāyāmṛta-taraṅgiṇī defending Vyāsatīrtha's Nyāyāmṛta against Madhusūdana Sarasvatī's Advaitasiddhi.
notes: A story that he first studied Advaita under Madhusūdana before refuting him circulates in modern accounts — low confidence, not verified.

name: Vyāsatīrtha

realization_account.text: The tradition regards Vyāsatīrtha as a rebirth of Prahlāda (after Bāhlīka of the Mahābhārata), later reborn as Rāghavendra; it tells that he sat on the Vijayanagara throne to avert an inauspicious conjunction (kuhu-yoga) that threatened the king, and that he installed 732 images of Hanumān.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The foremost dialectician of Dvaita and rājaguru of the Vijayanagara court (under Kṛṣṇadevarāya). His Nyāyāmṛta, Tarkatāṇḍava and Tātparyacandrikā ('the three of Vyāsa') attack Advaita, Navya-Nyāya and rival readings of the Brahmasūtras; the Nyāyāmṛta drew Madhusūdana Sarasvatī's Advaitasiddhi in reply. A composer of Kannada songs, he was the teacher of the Haridāsas Purandara Dāsa and Kanaka Dāsa, and of Vijayīndra Tīrtha. His brindāvana is at Nava Brindāvana near Hampi.

name: Vyomaśiva

scholarly.text: c. 10th c. CE (some place him earlier)

summary: Author of the Vyomavatī, the oldest extant commentary on the Padārthadharmasaṅgraha; a Śaiva ācārya.

name: Yadu
summary: Ancestor-king of the Yādavas who questions a carefree young avadhūta brāhmaṇa about the source of his peace and hears of his twenty-four teachers (Bhāgavata 11.7.25-11.9.33).

realization_account.text: Hearing the avadhūta, Yadu became free of all attachment and even-minded (Bhāgavata 11.9.33).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Yājñavalkya
summary: In the Mokṣadharma (12.298–306) Yājñavalkya teaches king Daivarāti Janaka the evolution of the principles, the guṇas, yoga and dissolution, tells how he won the Yajus teaching from the Sun by austerity (12.306.3–22), and relates his answers to the Gandharva Viśvāvasu (12.306.27); he declares that knowledge may be received even from a śūdra (12.306.85).
notes: U05's contribution (the epic account); the Upaniṣadic Yājñavalkya is covered by U03.

name: Yama
summary: Lord of death; in U06's texts the speaker of the Yama Gītās (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.7; Narasiṃha Purāṇa 8; Agni Purāṇa 381, the last addressed to Naciketas).
alt_summary: Lord of the dead; in the Sāvitrī episode he takes Satyavat's life and, pleased by Sāvitrī's words, returns it (3.281); in the Jāpaka story he appears with Kāla and Mṛtyu (12.192–193).
notes: U05's contribution; Yama as Naciketas's teacher in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad is covered by U03.

name: Yāmunācārya
notes: Contribution from U08 (Pāñcarātra defence); U14 owns his Vedānta.
summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava teacher (Āḷavantār), grand-teacher of Rāmānuja, whose Āgamaprāmāṇya defends the Pāñcarātra as valid scripture spoken by the Lord himself.
alt_summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava teacher, author of the Gītārthasaṅgraha summarizing the Gītā in 32 verses.

name: Yogarāja
summary: Disciple of Kṣemarāja; author of the commentary (Vivṛti) on the Paramārthasāra.

name: Yudhiṣṭhira (Dharmarāja)

tradition.text: end of the Dvāpara yuga (the Bhārata war; Kali yuga traditionally from 3102 BCE)

summary: Eldest Pāṇḍava, son of Dharma; answers the Yakṣa (3.297) and Nahuṣa (3.177), defends acting righteously without seeking its fruit against Draupadī (3.32.4), wishes to renounce after the war and is persuaded to rule (12.7–36), receives Bhīṣma's instruction, and at the end refuses to enter heaven without the dog who was devoted to him (17.3).
